question:
An investigator is studying physiologic renal responses to common medical conditions. She measures urine osmolalities in different parts of the nephron of a human subject in the emergency department. The following values are obtained:
Portion of nephron Osmolality (mOsmol/kg)
Proximal convoluted tubule 300
Loop of Henle, descending limb 1200
Loop of Henle, ascending limb 250
Distal convoluted tubule 100
Collecting duct 1200
These values were most likely obtained from an individual with which of the following condition?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Proximal convoluted tubule osmolality of 300 -> Indicates isotonic urine -> Loop of Henle descending limb osmolality of 1200 -> Suggests high concentration due to water reabsorption -> Ascending limb osmolality of 250 -> Indicates dilution due to active transport of Na+ -> Distal convoluted tubule osmolality of 100 -> Suggests further dilution -> Collecting duct osmolality of 1200 -> Indicates high concentration due to ADH action -> Consistent with dehydration -> 85%

CHAIN: Proximal convoluted tubule osmolality of 300 -> Indicates isotonic urine -> Loop of Henle descending limb osmolality of 1200 -> Suggests high concentration due to water reabsorption -> Ascending limb osmolality of 250 -> Indicates dilution due to active transport of Na+ -> Distal convoluted tubule osmolality of 100 -> Suggests further dilution -> Collecting duct osmolality of 1200 -> Indicates high concentration due to ADH action -> Unlikely in Gitelman syndrome -> 70%

analysis: The urine osmolality values indicate a significant concentration in the loop of Henle's descending limb (1200 mOsmol/kg) and collecting duct (1200 mOsmol/kg), while the ascending limb and distal convoluted tubule show much lower osmolalities (250 and 100 mOsmol/kg, respectively). This pattern suggests that the nephron is functioning to concentrate urine effectively, which is consistent with a state of dehydration. In dehydration, the body conserves water, leading to concentrated urine. Other conditions listed, such as Gitelman syndrome, psychogenic polydipsia, furosemide overdose, and diabetes insipidus, would not typically present with such high osmolality in the collecting duct and descending limb under normal circumstances.
